# Quenvira — demonstration guide

Your business, running smoothly.

This fictional workspace demonstrates workflows relevant to small UK cleaning companies. It is not affiliated with CleanFlo. No real customer, employee, access-code or health information should be entered.

1. Open Jobs on the fixed demo date, 20 October 2026.
2. Open Seabreeze Apartments, assigned to Maya Ellis. Start the job.
3. Tick the four quality checks and save an invented visit note. Complete the visit.
4. Create a draft invoice. At 20% demo VAT, £180 net becomes £216 total.
5. Record a manual demo payment. No money is collected or message sent.
6. Open Customers, add a fictional customer and use an example.com email address.
7. Plan three weekly visits from 3 November. Assign a free staff member. Deliberately overlap another booking to try the conflict guard.
8. Preview a staff role to see assigned jobs. This selector is not secure authentication.
9. In Demo & settings, export fictional customer/invoice CSVs or a JSON snapshot.
10. Reload to check browser persistence, then reset if desired.

The starting schedule illustrates a busy sample week; its repeat labels are examples, not a reconstructed historical recurrence series. New recurring bookings create exactly the number of visits requested, up to twelve. Edits and cancellations affect one visit only.

Changes are local to this browser. JSON snapshots are downloads only; restore/import is not available. Use one editing tab. A stale-tab check blocks detected overwrites, but is not transactional concurrency control. A storage failure leaves changes in memory and shows a warning. Clearing browser data loses edits.

The clock is intentionally fixed. Invoice and payment dates therefore use the demo date. Invoice downloads are text drafts, not valid tax invoices. No email, SMS, card processing or accounting integration is connected.

Before real use: server authentication, tenant isolation, persistent transactional storage, backup restoration, legal/privacy processes, tested deployment and real-device acceptance must be completed. This is a review demonstration, not a production-ready service.
